newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks slip in quiet pre-holiday trade.
newsitem.headline: French stocks slip in quiet pre-holiday trade.

text.p: French stocks opened a tick higher on Tuesday but quickly turned lower, pressured by weaker bond prices and a lower close on Wall Street, brokers said.
Activity was extremely thin, as many markets including Frankfurt's bourse were closed for New Year's Eve. London and New York were scheduled to close early.
Volume was a thin 470 million francs in the first 35 minutes of trading.
"From here until the expiry of futures and options (at 1500 GMT), it should be extremely quiet," one trader said.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index was down 4.75 points, or 0.2 percent, at 2,313.88 at 0945 GMT after opening at 2,323.87. It has risen 23 percent since the start of the year.
The CAC-40 futures contract was down five points at 2,314.
Among the CAC-40, Societe Generale's stock was down 1.75 percent at 560 francs. One trader said the issue was being penalised in year-end window-dressing after having underperformed during 1996.

Shares in Channel Tunnel operator Eurotunnel were down 1.42 percent at 6.95 francs. A Eurostar train with 469 passengers suffered engine failure on Monday and was stranded in the tunnel for nearly three hours before being towed out.

Among the secondary shares, Sylea was up 4.67 percent at 560 francs. The car parts manufacturer does a lot of its business with Italy's Fiat, whose shares rallied in Milan after the government decided to introduce incentives to car buyers to stimulate the flagging industry.
